description: The relations family fed by live LogQL against lgtm-loki. A metric query returns the same frame shape Prometheus does — one frame per series, endpoints in labels — so the same two routes apply: a ranged query with an empty Transform tab, and an instant query reshaped with organize + rowsToFields for per-edge ids. The flows are where the stack's own log lines come from: which service, which logger, which level.

options.content:
# Loki → relations charts

Alloy tails all five containers' stdout over the Docker socket and pushes it to **`lgtm-loki`** with no parsing pipeline at all (`lgtm/config/alloy.alloy`), because the services log in three different dialects. What that leaves to work with:

| carrier | where it comes from | values here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `service_name` | stream label, from the Compose service name — the same value Prometheus puts on that container's metrics and OTel puts on its spans | `grafana`, `loki`, `tempo`, `prometheus`, `alloy` |
| `detected_level` | **structured metadata**, written by Loki's own level detection — no parser needed | `info`, `warn`, `error`, `debug`, `unknown` |
| `logger` | a logfmt field, so it needs `\| logfmt` first; Grafana sets it, the dskit services mostly do not | `migrator`, `authn.service`, `tsdb.loki`, … |
| `job` | set by Alloy on every stream: `lgtm/docker` | — |

Use `{job="lgtm/docker"}` as the selector rather than `{stack=…}`: Alloy sets `stack` from the **Compose project name**, which is `grafana-echarts-panel-lgtm-3010` and changes with the port, while Prometheus's own external label happens to be the bare `lgtm`. Two different values for the same idea, in the same stack.

### A LogQL metric query is byte-identical to a Prometheus one

```logql
sum by (source, target) (
  count_over_time({job="lgtm/docker"} | label_format source=service_name, target=detected_level | target != "" [$__auto])
)
```

That returns `timeseries-multi` — one frame per series, `[Time, Value]`, the grouping labels on `Value` — exactly what a Prometheus range query returns. So everything on the Prometheus dashboard applies unchanged, including the choice of route:

- **Route A**, above: `label_format` renames the pair to the contract's own `source` / `target` keys, every frame passes the reader's edge test on its own, and the Transform tab stays empty. All the marks share the field name `Value`, so none of them is individually addressable.
- **Route B**: an instant query that also builds the id in LogQL — `label_format edge=` with a template — then `organize` + `rowsToFields`, giving one named field per edge.

`label_format` is the LogQL equivalent of Prometheus's `label_replace`, and its rename form (`dst=src`) is what makes Route A a one-liner. Note that it **also** works on structured metadata, which is why `detected_level` needs no parser: `| logfmt` is only there when a *logfmt field* like `logger` is wanted.

**A quiet stack is a flat dashboard.** These counts are real log lines from five containers doing their normal work — the boot-time spike from `migrator` will dominate any window that includes a restart.

panels.title: Route A — service → level, no transformations
panels.description:
Where each service's log lines land, by severity. One ranged LogQL query, an empty Transform tab, `label_format` doing the whole conversion.

A sankey is the right variant because the flow is **conserved**: every line a service emits has exactly one detected level, so a service's outgoing ribbons sum to its total volume and the `info` band is honestly comparable with the `error` one. `Sum` is the reducer, not `Last`: a `count_over_time` series is a count *per bucket*, and the interesting number over the window is the total.

Bipartite, so acyclic, so nothing is dropped — a level is never a service.

Node values are deliberately off. This response is edges only — no query returns a per-service total — so a node has no field of its own and the reader falls back to its **degree**: `grafana 5` would mean five edges, not five log lines. The Tempo dashboard is the one place on this stack where node values are real, because Tempo ships a `Nodes` frame.

panels.title: Route B — service → logger, with per-edge ids
panels.description:
The instant route, with the id built in LogQL rather than by a transformation:

```logql
| label_format src=service_name, dst=logger
| label_format edge=`{{.src}}-->{{.dst}}`
```

A second `label_format` stage can template over labels the first stage just created, so `edge` is a real label by the time `sum by (edge, src, dst)` runs — and `Format: instant` then makes it a column. `organize` moves `edge` to position 0 and renames `src` / `dst` to `source` / `target`; `rowsToFields` turns each row into a field named `grafana-->migrator`.

The query names the pair `src` / `dst` on purpose. A LogQL query that emits `source` and `target` *columns* is claimed as the legacy row format by the conversion the plugin registers above the panel on Grafana 13.2+, and the panel then shows **No data**. Renaming in the Transform tab runs after that pre-pass, so it is safe everywhere.

The `byName` override on `grafana-->migrator` is the payoff: on Route A that mark is called `Value`, like every other edge, and this override would paint all of them.

targets.expr:
topk(12,
  sum by (edge, src, dst) (
    count_over_time(
      {job="lgtm/docker"} | logfmt
        | label_format src=service_name, dst=logger
        | dst != ""
        | label_format edge=`{{.src}}-->{{.dst}}`
      [$__range]
    )
  )
)

panels.title: Three tiers from two queries — grafana → logger → level
panels.description:
Two ranged queries in one panel, neither transformed. The reader collects **every** frame that looks like edges, across queries — something no core transformation can do, since there is nothing to join on — so refId A's `service → logger` edges and refId B's `logger → level` edges land in one link list and the sankey lays them out as three columns.

Both queries are scoped to `service_name="grafana"`, which is not cosmetic: **Grafana is the only service in this stack that sets a `logger` field.** Unscoped, `| logfmt` over five services in three dialects puts mis-parsed `caller` values in the middle column. The second tier keys on `detected_level` rather than the parsed `level` for the same reason — Alloy writes `level=INFO` and Grafana writes `level=info`, which are two nodes for one idea, while Loki's own detection lower-cases both.

**Bounded by a `logger =~` allow-list rather than by `topk`.** Two facts force that. `topk(N, …)` in a ranged query is evaluated at every step, so what you get is the union of each bucket's top N — thirty-odd middle nodes over an hour, not six. And Loki has no instant form to escape into: an instant LogQL query returns a single flat frame whose label columns are *columns*, so the value field carries no labels and the reader finds no edges at all (that is exactly why Route B needs `organize` + `rowsToFields`). An explicit allow-list is stable across the window and honest about being a choice.

The tiers nearly conserve: the shortfall between a logger's inbound and outbound ribbons is lines whose level Loki could not detect.

This is also the panel to watch after a restart: `migrator` and `authn.service` dominate the boot window and then go quiet.

targets.expr:
sum by (source, target) (
  count_over_time(
    {job="lgtm/docker", service_name="grafana"} | logfmt
      | logger =~ `migrator|authn.service|resource-migrator|tsdb.loki|context|backgroundsvcs.managerAdapter`
      | label_format source=service_name, target=logger
      | target != ""
    [$__auto]
  )
)

sum by (source, target) (
  count_over_time(
    {job="lgtm/docker", service_name="grafana"} | logfmt
      | logger =~ `migrator|authn.service|resource-migrator|tsdb.loki|context|backgroundsvcs.managerAdapter`
      | label_format source=logger, target=detected_level
      | target != ""
    [$__auto]
  )
)

panels.title: Service × level as a matrix — chord
panels.description:
The same query as the top-left panel, drawn as a chord. Over a bipartite pair a chord is a **matrix view** rather than a reciprocity view: no arc has ribbons in both directions, so what it adds over the sankey is that each arc's *own* total is a visible length — a service's whole log volume and a level's whole share are on the same ring, at the same scale.

`error` and `warn` keep the fixed colours from the sankey's overrides, addressed by regex on the target end of the edge id. On Route A that regex matches the field's **display name** (the rendered legend format), which is why the ids have to be written into `legendFormat` even though nothing else here reads them.

panels.title: The lines behind the counts
panels.description:
The same selector the charts aggregate, unaggregated. Worth having on the dashboard: every number above is a count of these lines, and the three dialects the header mentions are visible here — Grafana's `logger=…` logfmt, dskit's `caller=…`, and Alloy's own output.

Loki's derived field turns any `traceID=` in a line into a link into `lgtm-tempo`, so a log line from a query path opens the trace that produced it.
